content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged axolotl frame. Host frame: the axolotl sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining an axolotl and a Chinese pangolin. Head of the axolotl, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: axolotl body and legs, with its own smooth, moist skin on the face and belly, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the Chinese pangolin, as parts and materials on the axolotl's own body: large overlapping keratin scales in its own colors, grown from the skin as the axolotl's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, hips, legs and tail; it replaces the axolotl's smooth, moist skin there and conforms to the axolotl's body, each scale sized to the axolotl's own body segments and muscle masses, one scale per segment or muscle mass; every covered part keeps the axolotl's own length and shape, and the tail stays the axolotl's own tail; the smooth, moist skin stops at the covering's edge, and the face and belly keep the axolotl's own smooth, moist skin. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (river forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Building hybrid creature silhouette**
I'm shaping a single silhouette that uses an axolotl as the host frame, with its head, body, and legs defining the outline, and layering large overlapping pangolin scales over the crown and neck while keeping the face smooth and the eyes clear.
**Planning hybrid creature image**
I'm organizing the hybrid design details—pangolin scales over an axolotl body, bilateral symmetry, river-forest countershading, and natural-history illustration style—before preparing the 1:1 image.
**Researching axolotl reference details**
I'm gathering axolotl reference details to inform the hybrid creature design, focusing on anatomy, texture, and color so the next image concept stays accurate and visually cohesive.
**Building natural history illustration**
I'm preparing a side three-quarter natural history illustration that blends an axolotl body with pangolin scales across the crown, neck, back, flanks, hips, legs, and tail, keeping the face and belly smooth against a plain light background.
